citation.description: Operator ruling comment (2026-08-07) by RebarBotNava explicitly states: 'WORKING AS INTENDED — closing as not_a_bug. The ticket's premise is rejected. Failing a close on an unmet or unmeetable acceptance criterion is INTENDED behaviour, not a gate defect.' The ruling clearly records that the gate SHOULD NOT gain N/A vocabulary.

criteria.criterion: A ruling is recorded on whether the close gate should gain an N/A / not-applicable criterion vocabulary. IT SHOULD NOT — see the operator ruling comment on this ticket.

citation.description: Operator ruling comment (2026-08-07) states verbatim: 'an AC nobody can satisfy is a signal the plan was written wrong, and surfacing that at close time is the gate doing its job. An N/A marker would convert that signal into a checkbox.' The rationale is captured in the ticket comment.

criteria.criterion: The rationale is captured: an AC nobody can satisfy is a signal the PLAN was written wrong, and surfacing that at close time is the gate working. An N/A marker would convert that signal into a checkbox and weaken the gate exactly where it is most valuable.

citation.description: Operator ruling comment (2026-08-07) states: 'Standing guidance this establishes: when a close fails on an AC that cannot be satisfied as written, rewrite the AC to state what is actually verifiable, then close normally. --force-close remains the operator's escape hatch, but it is not the routine answer to an unmeetable AC.' This exactly matches the criterion.

criteria.criterion: The standing alternative is stated for AC authors: rewrite the unmeetable criterion to say what is actually verifiable, then close normally. `--force-close` remains an operator escape hatch, not the routine answer.
